subject: Re: Q4 capacity & renewal — proposal to keep Shoply on Redwood
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena@shoply.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-02T09:12:00Z
Subject: Q4 capacity & renewal

Jordan —

We’re coming up on our annual renewal and the teams here have been asked to validate long-term capacity and unit cost. We’ve had a demo from CloudStride and they’re pushing a significant price discount if we replatform. Before we get pulled into a full bake-off, can you share a short plan for:

- How Redwood would prove parity/perf on our peak queries (benchmarks we can run)
- A winback/upgrade offer to cover the next 12–18 months (capacity + price)
- Any operational changes you’d do to avoid a migration (cutover risk)

I’m cc’ing procurement. We want something practical to present to the execs this week.

Thanks,
Elena Soto
Head of Platform, Shoply
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena@shoply.com>
Cc: procurement@shoply.com
Date: 2027-11-02T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Q4 capacity & renewal

Elena —

Thanks for the heads up and the context — appreciate the directness. We can absolutely do a focused, time-boxed bake-off plan that minimizes your engineering lift. High level we propose:

1) 48-hour benchmark run using your representative traffic (we’ll take a 2‑hour sample and synthesize peak arrivals). Redwood will supply measurement scripts and provide a side-by-side latency/cost/95th-percentile report.

2) A temporary capacity uplift (reserved burst slots) for 90 days while we tune model profiles + KV cache.

3) A one-time credit + short-term term-adjusted rate for committed uplift to bridge pricing while you evaluate.

I’ll pull together details and loop in Ben (pricing) and Monica (solutions) for the execution plan — sending a draft by EOD tomorrow. Would you be available for a 30-minute call Wed 11/4?

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-03T08:31:00Z
Subject: Re: Shoply — initial save offer

Team —

Quick notes after review of Shoply’s usage:
- Typical peak sequences are short (avg seq len ~ 48 tokens) but high QPS during promos. We can measurably reduce token cost with prefix caching + tuned batching.
- Pricing: I can approve up to a 22% one-year concession on new committed uplift if we tie it to an ARR minimum. Anything deeper needs RevOps/legal signoff.
- Offer idea: 3-month free burst credits (to verify perf) + a 12-month term at the concession rate for the uplifted capacity. Include a rollback clause so Shoply can reduce baseline after 12 months if KPIs miss target.

I’ll draft the numbers for Jordan to include in the external proposal.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Sales — Enterprise
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-04T16:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Shoply benchmark plan (attachments)

Jordan/Ben —

Attached are: 1) the benchmark script we’ll run against Shoply sample traces (shoply-bench-20271105.pdf), 2) the setup runbook for the 48-hour run (shoply-setup-runbook.xlsx). I also included an internal checklist for the ops handoff.

Notes for the customer call tomorrow: emphasize the low effort required on their side (we’ll synthesize traffic from their 2-hr export). Call prep: 11/05 10:30am ET confirmed with Elena.

—Monica
Senior Solutions Engineer
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena@shoply.com>, procurement@shoply.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-05T13:05:00Z
Subject: Shoply — benchmark plan & provisional offer

Elena —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, attached is the benchmark plan and a provisional commercial term sheet (shoply-save-offer-terms.pdf). Summary:

- Execution: 48-hour benchmark starting 11/08. Minimal sample export required (we’ll take care of traffic replay).
- Capacity: reserved burst for 90 days to match peak QPS.
- Commercial: 22% uplift concession on the additional committed capacity for 12 months + 3 months of burst credits to validate.
- Safety: rollback clause after 12 months if latency/cost targets not met; we commit to an SLA uplift for peak days.

Attachments: benchmark plan, provisional term sheet, runbook. Please review and tell me if procurement needs any additional artifacts (SOC2 snapshot, audit logs access, etc.). If this aligns, we’ll start the benchmark next Tuesday 11/08.

Best,
Jordan
From: Elena Soto <elena@shoply.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@shoply.com
Date: 2027-11-09T17:46:00Z
Subject: Re: Shoply — benchmark plan & provisional offer

Jordan / team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the detailed plan. The benchmark artifacts look good — procurement asked for the provisional term sheet formatted as a redline-ready PDF, so the attached doc works. Two notes from execs: CloudStride’s discounted ask is aggressive and their proposal is heavier on price than ops guarantees.

We’ll run the benchmark. If Redwood proves parity on latency and cost-per-call in the 48-hour window, we’ll move forward with the uplift and the concessioned term for 12 months. Please also prepare the SOC2 attestation and the sample audit log export for procurement.

One last ask: can you include a short migration-risk memo (one page) that we can forward to the CTO comparing expected cutover effort vs. staying on Redwood? That will help us make the case.

I’ll queue the benchmark for 11/08 as agreed.

—Elena
Head of Platform, Shoply
